What fleetd's agents can do, what they can't, and the limits fleetd enforces.

Every agent is a Claude Code session. fleetd adds its own tools to it, which Claude Code shows as `mcp__fleetd__<tool>`. The workspace checks every call, whatever the agent was told.

## Who gets which tools

- **The lead**: one per bot. It talks with you in the bot's chat and starts the bot's agents.
- **Agents**: writers, which change code on a branch of their own; readers, which look into something and report; reviewers, which review a PR; QA agents, which test a PR. They can't start agents of their own.

Each tool below says when only one of them gets it.

## fleetd's tools

### Working with agents

- <span id="spawn_agent"></span>`spawn_agent`: Start an agent. Lead only.
- <span id="message_agent"></span>`message_agent`: Send an agent a message, while it runs or after it ended. Lead only.
- <span id="stop_agent"></span>`stop_agent`: Stop an agent. Lead only.
- <span id="agents"></span>`agents`: List the bot's agents, with each one's state, branch and PR.
- <span id="agent_messages"></span>`agent_messages`: Read what the agents wrote to each other. Lead only.
- <span id="agent_message"></span>`agent_message`: Write to other agents of the bot. Agents only.
- <span id="ask_lead"></span>`ask_lead`: Ask the lead a question. Agents only.
- <span id="brief_read"></span>`brief_read`: Read the goal and limits of its work. Agents only.
- <span id="report"></span>`report`: Record a review's verdict. Agents only.
- <span id="wait_ci"></span>`wait_ci`: Wait for CI to finish, or a PR to merge, then carry on. Agents only.
- <span id="review_read"></span>`review_read`: Read the review findings on its PRs.
- <span id="change_enqueue"></span>`change_enqueue`: Put a PR on the merge train. Lead only.

### Orders and decisions

- <span id="brief"></span>`brief`: Open an order: its goal, why, and when it's done. Lead only.
- <span id="close"></span>`close`: Close an order once it's done. Lead only.
- <span id="checklist"></span>`checklist`: Keep the to-do list shown beside the chat, and say where things stand for the chat list. Lead only.
- <span id="decide"></span>`decide`: Record a decision, so it's never asked twice. Lead only.
- <span id="decisions_search"></span>`decisions_search`: Search the bot's decisions.
- <span id="nudge"></span>`nudge`: Flag its last message for you to look at. Lead only.

### Memory

- <span id="remember"></span>`remember`: Remember something for later sessions: about the bot, or about how you work. Lead only.
- <span id="forget"></span>`forget`: Remove something it remembered. Lead only.
- <span id="memory_read"></span>`memory_read`: Read one memory topic. Lead only.

### Automations

- <span id="automation_create"></span>`automation_create`: Make an automation that runs on a schedule, or once at a set time. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_list"></span>`automation_list`: List the bot's automations. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_update"></span>`automation_update`: Change, pause or resume an automation. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_delete"></span>`automation_delete`: Delete an automation. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_run"></span>`automation_run`: Run an automation now. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_runs"></span>`automation_runs`: List an automation's runs. Lead only.
- <span id="automation_confirm"></span>`automation_confirm`: Ask you to let an automation run on its own. Lead only.

### Chat and files

- <span id="chat_search"></span>`chat_search`: Search the bot's chat. Lead only.
- <span id="chat_read"></span>`chat_read`: Read the messages around one chat message. Lead only.
- <span id="chat_file"></span>`chat_file`: Post a file in the chat, such as a screenshot.
- <span id="publish_artifact"></span>`publish_artifact`: Publish a report that opens beside the chat.
- <span id="share_port"></span>`share_port`: Share a dev server it started as a link only the workspace's members open. Agents only.
- <span id="artifact_read"></span>`artifact_read`: Read a published report.
- <span id="attachment_read"></span>`attachment_read`: Open a file you attached.

### Bots and repos

- <span id="project_setup"></span>`project_setup`: Set up its bot: instructions, setup commands and variables, when you ask. Lead only.
- <span id="repo_add"></span>`repo_add`: Add a repo to its bot, when you ask. Lead only.
- <span id="repo_create"></span>`repo_create`: Make a new GitHub repo for its bot, once you say yes. Lead only.
- <span id="repo_remove"></span>`repo_remove`: Take a repo out of its bot, when you ask. Lead only.
- <span id="project_propose"></span>`project_propose`: Propose a new bot, which you create on its card. Lead only.
- <span id="project_message"></span>`project_message`: Write to another bot's lead. Lead only.
- <span id="factory_status"></span>`factory_status`: See how the other bots are doing. Lead only.
- <span id="skill_install"></span>`skill_install`: Install skills from skills.sh for the bot. Lead only.
- <span id="skill_save"></span>`skill_save`: Save a skill it wrote. Lead only.
- <span id="usage_resume"></span>`usage_resume`: Lift a Claude usage pause on the bot's machine. Lead only.

### Approvals and secrets

- <span id="request_secret"></span>`request_secret`: Ask you for a secret, such as an API key. It sees only a fingerprint. Lead only.
- <span id="request_withdraw"></span>`request_withdraw`: Take back a request it no longer needs. Lead only.
- <span id="gated_run"></span>`gated_run`: Run a risky command, once you approve it. Lead only.
- <span id="confirm_step"></span>`confirm_step`: Click a final Confirm or Submit on a site, by the bot's approval mode. Lead only.

### Screens

- <span id="session_start"></span>`session_start`: Open a screen: a browser, a phone or a desktop.
- <span id="desktop"></span>`desktop`: Click, type and scroll on a desktop screen.
- <span id="session_end"></span>`session_end`: Close its screen.
- <span id="request_takeover"></span>`request_takeover`: Ask you to take over its screen, for a captcha, a passkey or a device approval.

### Vault and payments

- <span id="vault_items"></span>`vault_items`: List the vault items it may use, never their values.
- <span id="vault_store"></span>`vault_store`: Save a secret it holds as a new variable of its bot, never showing the value.
- <span id="fill_credential"></span>`fill_credential`: Fill a login field from the vault, without seeing it.
- <span id="request_sign_in"></span>`request_sign_in`: Sign in to a site: from the vault, else through a secure form you fill in, saved to the vault.
- <span id="fill_address"></span>`fill_address`: Fill an address form from the vault.
- <span id="vault_import_search"></span>`vault_import_search`: Search your 1Password for items to import into the vault. Lead only.
- <span id="vault_import_propose"></span>`vault_import_propose`: Propose 1Password items for you to import. Lead only.
- <span id="purchase_request"></span>`purchase_request`: Record a payment at a checkout, with the card you picked. Lead only.
- <span id="purchase_fill"></span>`purchase_fill`: Fill the card into the checkout, without seeing it. Lead only.
- <span id="request_secure_input"></span>`request_secure_input`: Ask you for a value it must never see, such as a passport number. Lead only.
- <span id="secure_input_fill"></span>`secure_input_fill`: Fill that value into its field. Lead only.

## Limits

The workspace enforces these on every call, whatever an agent was told.

- Only a lead starts agents (`spawn_agent`), and agents can't start their own.
- A lead has at most 32 agents open at once, or twice the bot's max agents when that is more.
- How many agents run at once is capped per bot (Max agents in the chat) and per machine (Settings › Workspace › Machines; unset, what the machine fits, at most 64). More wait and start by themselves. The lead doesn't count.
- A command of class `irreversible`, `money` or `credential` goes through `gated_run`: it runs only after you approve it, for at most 4 hours.

These limits cover calls to fleetd, not the agent's own shell, which can do what your OS user can. See [What an agent can reach](/docs/security#agent-reach).

## Claude Code tools

As listed by Claude Code 2.1.302. fleetd is tested with 2.1.314.

**Allowed:** `Bash`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Skill`, `ToolSearch`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Write`.

A bot's [`.fleetd/policy.yaml`](/docs/config-and-files#policy) can block more with `tools.deny`.

### Blocked everywhere

No session fleetd starts gets these, and your own settings can't turn them back on.

- `Task`, `Agent`: fleetd starts and tracks every agent itself, with spawn_agent. Task and Agent are one tool: blocking either removes both.
- `Workflow`, `ListAgents`, `SendMessage`, `TaskStop`, `TaskOutput`, `TeamCreate`, `TeamDelete`: fleetd starts and tracks every agent itself, with spawn_agent.
- `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`: Nobody sits at a terminal to answer it, so the run would stall. Agents ask through fleetd instead.
- `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `CronList`, `ScheduleWakeup`: fleetd schedules work itself, so a restart can't lose it.
- `EnterWorktree`, `ExitWorktree`: fleetd gives each writer its own worktree. A session that moves to another folder can't be resumed.
- `Bash(claude *)` and 20 more rules like it: A claude started inside a session would run outside fleetd's limits, on any model. Agents start agents with spawn_agent.

  <details><summary>All 21 rules</summary>

  `Bash(claude *)`, `Bash(/*/claude *)`, `Bash(~/*/claude *)`, `Bash($HOME/*/claude *)`, `Bash(./*/claude *)`, `Bash(/*/claude/versions/*)`, `Bash(~/*/claude/versions/*)`, `Bash($HOME/*/claude/versions/*)`, `Bash(npx claude *)`, `Bash(bunx claude *)`, `Bash(npx *@anthropic-ai/claude-code*)`, `Bash(bunx *@anthropic-ai/claude-code*)`, `Bash(npm exec *@anthropic-ai/claude-code*)`, `Bash(pnpm dlx *@anthropic-ai/claude-code*)`, `Bash(sh -*c *claude -*)`, `Bash(bash -*c *claude -*)`, `Bash(zsh -*c *claude -*)`, `Bash(/*sh -*c *claude -*)`, `Bash(env *claude -*)`, `Bash(exec *claude -*)`, `Bash(xargs *claude -*)`

  </details>


A tool like these that a newer Claude Code adds is blocked too: a session that still offers one is stopped, and later sessions on that machine block it.

### Blocked for fleetd's agents

Your own threads keep these.

- `ReportFindings` (leads and agents): Agents report a review with fleetd's own `report`.
- `DesignSync`, `NotebookEdit` (leads and agents): fleetd's agents don't use it, and every tool adds to each request.
- `Bash(git push *--no-verify*)`, `Bash(git *core.hooksPath*)`, `Bash(git *core.hookspath*)` (agents): A writer may push only after the repo's pre-push check passed (`.fleetd/pre-push.json`). A person's push can still skip it.
- `Edit`, `Write` (leads with repos): A lead with repos never changes files: its agents do. A lead with no repo keeps them.
- `WebFetch`, `WebSearch` (leads with repos): A lead with repos has its agents read the web; a lead with no repo keeps it.

### What a lead does without asking

A lead runs in Claude Code's `manual` permission mode, with no sandbox ([how leads run](/docs/security#how-leads-run)). Its shell commands run without asking, unless one would wipe the machine. These run without asking too:

- `Read`: A lead reads what the person can, as under full access.
- `Edit`: A lead that does its own work writes what the person can; a lead with repos has no Edit.
- `Write`: A lead that does its own work writes what the person can; a lead with repos has no Write.
- `WebSearch`: A search sends only its query, to the search provider.
- `Skill`: Loads a skill's instructions; runs nothing.
- `mcp__fleetd`: fleetd's own tools. The workspace checks every call.
- `Bash(agent-device *)`: Phone screens work for a lead as for any agent. A final Send or Pay is the person's, through request_takeover.

These go through the bot's approval mode first:

- `WebFetch`: A lead fetches a site unasked only once the person allowed or linked it.
- `mcp__fleetd__confirm_step`: A final Confirm on a site goes through the bot's approval mode, like a send.
- `mcp__fleetd__automation_confirm`: Only the person lets an automation run on its own, on its card.
- `mcp__fleetd__project_propose`: Only a person creates a bot, on the card a lead's proposal shows them.

## Settings fleetd sets

In the environment of every claude fleetd starts, unless a line says otherwise. Those marked *forced* are in fleetd's own settings for the session too, so the `env` in your Claude Code settings can't change them.

- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` = `1` (*forced*): Turns off background jobs in Bash: one would outlive the turn fleetd tracks.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS` = `1` (*forced*): Removes the Workflow tool: fleetd starts agents itself.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS` = `1` (*forced*): Removes the built-in Explore and Plan agents: fleetd starts agents itself.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW` = `1` (*forced*): Removes the built-in claude agent: fleetd starts agents itself.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` removed (*forced*): Agent teams: fleetd starts agents itself.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_COORDINATOR_MODE` removed (*forced*): Coordinator mode turns a session into one that only hands work to subagents.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` = `1`, and `autoMemoryEnabled: false` (*forced*): fleetd decides what each agent is told. Notes claude keeps per folder would carry stale text from one agent to the next.
- `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` = the default profile's model (`claude-opus-5-5` unless you chose another) (*forced*): claude's background calls (like session titles) use the default profile's model, not Haiku.
- `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` = `1` (*forced*): Keeps the claude version fleetd tested. An update mid-run would swap it under a live session.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS` = `1`: A failed start comes back as a result fleetd can read and show.
- `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` = `true`, unless your environment or `claude.env` sets it: Tools load when used, not on every request. fleetd's own tools always load at start.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, unless your environment or `claude.env` sets it (*forced*): How long the prompt cache lasts:
  - `1h` for leads with no repo: A lead with no repo waits between a person's messages.
  - `1h` for leads with repos: A lead often waits more than 5 minutes for reviews and CI. A longer cache saves rewriting its whole context.
  - `1h` for threads you start: Your own thread waits while you read and reply.
  - `5m` for agents: An agent works in one burst and ends, so a 1-hour cache would go unused.
- `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` = `280000` for agents, unless your environment or `claude.env` sets it (*forced*): No command outlives an agent's 5-minute prompt cache, which would cost a full rewrite of its context. Long test suites are CI's job.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_SILENT_TURN_REMINDER` = `0` for leads (*forced*): Turns off claude's mid-turn reminder to post an update. Only a lead turn's last text reaches the chat.
- `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT` removed: claude would treat the session as nested inside another one.

## Your own Claude Code setup

Sessions start on top of your own Claude Code setup on that machine.

- Your MCP servers, skills, plugins, hooks and `CLAUDE.md` load as in your own `claude`.
- Your allow and deny rules apply, but fleetd's blocks win.
- Your own subagents (`~/.claude/agents`) are listed, but nothing can start them.

To see exactly what a session was told, open the agent in the app and pick **What it was told**. On the workspace's machine, `fleetd prompts show --session <machine>/<thread>` prints it too.
